Broncos vs. Rams picks, prediction, player props: Expert's best bets for Sunday Night Football in NFL Week 3 Mile High altitude and a stout Denver defense give the underdog hosts a distinct edge against Los Angeles in a tight prime-time battle By Will Brinson Sep 27, 2026 at 8:07 pm ET • 3 min read Add CBS Sports on Google Imagn Images The NFL never disappoints, and Week 3 of the 2026 season appears to be no different. Just when we think we know everything, we know very little. Sunday Night Football will be a good test of how little we know, with the Broncos playing Jekyll and Hyde the first two weeks of the season and in the two different halves against the Jaguars last week. The total is down to 44.5. Bet on Sunday Night Football at DraftKings, where new users get $150 in bonus bets after they spend $5+: The Rams pulled a similar move in Week 1 versus Week 2, and now they're favored on the road in prime time in a really tough place to play early in the year. They opened with a loss to the 49ers but bounced back by cruising past the Giants 28-6 on Monday night in Week 2. Los Angeles is a 1.5-point favorite, and the Over/Under for total points is 44.5. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Best bets for Sunday Night Football Broncos +2.5 I'm *the* Rams guy -- we joked about what the number would need to be in order for me to NOT take the Rams on our SportsLine picks show Wednesday. And I was on the Rams earlier in the week, but I'm pivoting now, with me thinking the altitude plus the Broncos defense and the high level of this Denver team meaning that the Broncos probably shouldn't be underdogs at home this early in the year. Aaron Donald returned to the NFL last week and played a decent number of snaps, but it's going to be tough for him to ramp up at Mile High. Sean Payton can coach around the weaknesses of his team, and while I expect the Rams to very much keep this competitive and for it to a be a low-scoring close game, my spidey sense says the Broncos find a way to win late, and if not, it's a field goal walk-off situation for either team, making these points extremely valuable. Sunday Night Football player props Jaylen Waddle 6+ receptions (+127, DraftKings) You'll see the Over for Waddle's receptions above heavily juiced, but just know that we're playing his SIX reception number at +127 on DraftKings here. I like both, obviously, and think this is a good ladder spot for Waddle. In Week 1 he was non-existent, which is shocking given that the Broncos traded a first-round pick for him this offseason. Week 2 was very different and the Broncos reaped the benefits. I fully expect Davis Webb and Sean Payton to get Waddle heavily involved, especially since the Broncos running back depth chart is extremely depleted. Kyren Williams over 12.5 receiving yards (-116, DraftKings) Williams and Blake Corum are very much in a timeshare at running back at this point and I don't think that will change. It makes backing their rush props difficult. But it also means Williams receiving prop is way down. He's always good for several targets in the short-yardage area and 12.5 isn't that much to ask from the standout running back, especially when Denver's ability to bring pressure plus the likely absence of Puka Nacua meaning safety valves for Matthew Stafford will likely be a play-calling focus for McVay. Bet on NFL player props and more at BetMGM: Sunday Night Football anytime touchdowns Davante Adams (+115, DraftKings) Davante went off in Week 2 after a slow Week 1, and while this matchup is much more difficult for the superstar wide receiver, he's getting a fantastic price here on an anytime touchdown. The Broncos and Patrick Surtain will make life difficult, and I definitely don't see him chasing 200 receiving yards. But at plus money with his usage and red-zone scoring ability? This is a no-brainer. Bo Nix (+475, DraftKings) This number has me giddy! Bo Nix is almost 5-1 to score a touchdown??? Yeah the Rams defense is great and yeah Nix hasn't been running like we'd prefer with eight rushes for eight total yards. But he's always a threat to run and against this defense I think he'll take off a few more times. And I actually foresee some red-zone dial ups to activate his legs in tough spots, making this number extremely tantalizing. His first-touchdown-scorer number of 18-1 is real nice as well. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. This year, we are not faced with any uncertainty regarding the number one overall as Fernando Mendoza is set to head to Las Vegas as the new franchise cornerstone. After Mendoza, there is a lot of uncertainty as to how the rest of the first round unfolds. With that, let’s dive into the top prop bets available for the upcoming first round. Doc’s Sports offers NFL expert picks for every game on our NFL predictions page. Top 5 Pick: Sonny Styles Perhaps the most intriguing prop bet is whether or not Sonny Styles will be drafted inside the Top Five. My answer is yes. We know that Mendoza will go first overall, followed by either David Bailey or Arvell Reese. Whichever of the two isn’t drafted second, will almost certainly be taken third. That leaves the fourth and fifth selections by the Tennessee Titans and New York Giants. Both need help on defense; however, both would love to draft Jeremiyah Love. That said, the other will jump at the chance of drafting Styles. It is also quite possible that a team like the Dallas Cowboys make a big move to jump into the Top Five and draft Styles. It is highly unlikely he will fall outside the Top Five. My Pick: Yes, -110 First Wide Receiver Drafted The wide receiver class is deep, with Day 2 selections offering incredible value for teams who wait to jump at the position. Makai Lemon, Jordyn Tyson, and Carnell Tate are widely regarded as the best three wide receivers in this class. While all three will likely be taken inside the Top 15, Tate will be the first receiver off the board for this class. Tate reeled in 51 catches for 875 yards and nine touchdowns in his last season at Ohio State. While Lemon is a strong option in the slot, and Tyson is going to be an enticing red-zone threat, Tate is the most well-rounded receiver. Do not expect Tate to slide out of the Top 10. Based on Shough’s age and college profile, there is a possibility the market is overconfident in his abilities. Shough’s season passing total is currently lined within 200 yards of both Justin Herbert and Caleb Williams and 150 yards of Josh Allen , all quarterbacks with more NFL experience and a greater certainty that they will be starting in the league for seasons to come. Last season, Shough played against an extremely favorable slate of opposing defenses. Last year was considered a success for the rookie quarterback, but diving into the numbers raises some question marks for the Saints' passing attack. The Saints faced the 31st-ranked schedule of opposing passing defenses last season and are currently projected to face the 21st-ranked in 2026. In Shough’s nine starts, he faced one single team that finished the season with a winning record. Despite the soft schedule, the Saints dug themselves into early deficits, forcing Kellan Moore into heavier passing scripts. The Saints trailed at halftime in seven of nine games from Week 9 onward. In fact, the Saints led the league with the most offensive snaps while trailing. Although Shough wasn’t a complete garbage time merchant, he averaged 140 passing yards per game in the second half compared to 110 passing yards in the first half. An improved running game could help ease some of the need to rely on Shough as often as last year. The Saints finished 28th in total rushing yards and 31st in yards per rush in 2025 but were aggressive in signing running back Travis Etienne and guard David Edwards to help improve the run game. A better rushing attack can lead to a lower passing rate and create fewer clock stoppages, reducing Shough’s passing yardage ceiling. The Sharp Football season-long projections are more bullish on Shough compared to ESPN, but given the fragility of his profile, there is a good chance that Shough would need to start all 17 games to reach his season-long total. Last season, only 11 quarterbacks started 17 games, which provides a solid argument for betting season-long quarterback unders. In college, Shough did not start more than seven games in any of his first five seasons as he dealt with multiple different season-ending injuries. Betting overs on a sophomore quarterback, who was drafted after six seasons of college football, is probably not optimal. Given Shough’s injury history, there are probably multiple outs to cashing the under. Sean Payton, who is entering his third season in charge of the Broncos, has made the postseason in 11 of his 18 seasons as a head coach. He has never finished with fewer than seven wins, effectively putting his teams in playoff contention every single year dating back to 2006. Eight of his 11 playoff berths have coincided with division titles, too, including last year’s. Denver is sitting at +225 to repeat as AFC West champions, which is good for third behind both the Chiefs and Chargers. However, the Broncos actually account for 34% of the bets to win the AFC West, narrowly outpacing the Chiefs and Chargers’ respective 32%. And in terms of the total handle, Denver leads the pack at 40%, signifying a sharp lean in their favor. Analysis We are entering Year 3 of Sean Payton and Bo Nix, not to mention all the other returning skill position players. Denver also went out and added Jaylen Waddle to supplement Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin, Pat Bryant, Marvin Mims Jr., Lil’Jordan Humphrey, Evan Engram, J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. They also bring back most key contributors from their defense, even using their top draft pick on Tyler Onyedim to make up for lineman John Franklin-Myers leaving in free agency. Considering that unit held opponents to the third-fewest points per game last season, it’s easy to see them being elite again in 2026. Going against a Chargers squad that hasn’t won a division crown since 2009 and a Chiefs team that showed signs of age and injury in 2025, the Broncos should be in the driver’s seat once again in 2026. What is worth noting, however, is that they account for the third-fewest bets to miss the playoffs, as well as the smallest handle in that market. Basically, very few people and even fewer sharp bettors are banking on Los Angeles to miss the playoffs. Analysis Los Angeles went 11-6 in each of Jim Harbaugh’s first two seasons at the helm, earning a Wild Card berth both times. Dating back to Harbaugh’s time in charge of the 49ers, he has led his team to the playoffs in five of six opportunities. The Chargers also enter this campaign in a much healthier position than they were in last year, in which they thrived despite their offensive line issues. Pro Football Focus ranked their O-line 30th out of 32 units in the NFL, with Joe Alt missing 11 games and Rashawn Slater missing all 17. Their respective returns – plus the arrival of offensive guru Mike McDaniel at coordinator – could vault Justin Herbert into the league’s top tier of quarterbacks. Omarion Hampton might break out as well, if first round pick Jake Slaughter can replace the retired Bradley Bozeman and injured Tyler Biadasz at center. The Chargers have boasted a top-10 scoring defense in both of Harbaugh’s seasons, too, so there’s reason to believe they can weather the losses of Da’Shawn Hand and Otito Ogbonnia up front. But with Antonio Pierce and Pete Carroll gone and reigning Super Bowl champion offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak now in charge, things could be different in Vegas. On top of the general public support, there is a pretty substantial sharp lean in the Raiders’ favor. 91% of the handle is on the Raiders to clear 5.5 wins, which is about as close to universal support as you can get from a total money perspective. Analysis Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza may be at polar opposite ends of their careers, but their arrivals are reason for confidence in Las Vegas. The top rookie and seasoned veteran should fit nice into Kubiak’s system, which brought Sam Darnold back from the dead in Seattle. Although they may not have the weapons to cobble together an elite offense, the Raiders have Kolton Miller returning at left tackle and Tyler Linderbaum entering the fray at center. That should give them an O-line that PFF ranks higher than No. 32, like they did last season, beyond Kubiak’s offense traditionally minimizing talent deficiencies up front. The Raiders have the Browns, Cardinals and Titans on the schedule after Thanksgiving, at which point the team will probably have come into its own. Games against the Jets, Saints and Dolphins look winnable as well, to say nothing of any potential upsets. Keep an eye on Week 18 against the Chiefs, when Kansas City may have already locked up their playoff seeding. There is a massive sharp lean, however, with 43% of the handle on the under. So while the public as a whole is getting swept up in the hype for the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, the people putting more money behind their bets aren’t quite as convinced. Analysis While there is reason to believe the Raiders will take a leap forward in 2026, their new franchise quarterback might not have a lot to do with it. Cousins, who is freshly 38 years old, started 14 games in 2024 and appeared in 10 in 2025. He led Atlanta to a 12-10 record when he started, despite all of that coming after his 2023 Achilles surgery. Cousins posted an unimpressive 87.2 passer rating during his time with the Falcons, a noticeable decline from his 99.9 mark between 2015 and 2023, but he was still a steady enough veteran presence to start over Michael Penix Jr. when healthy. Based on the start of training camp and the preseason, the starting job in Las Vegas belongs to Cousins. The Raiders also have a pretty tough schedule through their Week 13 bye, which would make installing Mendoza particularly difficult. I think the rookie sees the field in 2026, but not in any serious capacity until the final five games.
